title: Do You Really Need a Locksmith to Copy a House Key? An Honest Answer
description: A San Francisco locksmith explains when a hardware store key copy is the smarter, cheaper choice, and when a locksmith visit is actually worth paying for.
intro: We get calls every week from people who want a locksmith to drive over and copy a house key. We are happy to do it, but we would rather tell you the truth first: for a standard house key, the hardware store down the street will usually do the job for a few dollars, while a mobile service call includes travel, arrival time and labor. After 30 years in this trade, and a father who was a locksmith before us, we believe a good locksmith should tell you when you do not need one.

sections.heading: A Standard House Key Copy Belongs at the Hardware Store
paragraphs: If you have a working key and you just want a spare, take it to the nearest hardware or home-improvement store. Most San Francisco neighborhoods have one within a short walk or drive. A basic copy of a common house key there usually costs somewhere around five to ten dollars and takes a few minutes while you wait.

When you order a mobile locksmith to your door for the same copy, you are paying for much more than the key: the drive across the city, parking, the technician's time and the service call itself. That makes sense when you need the locksmith on site. It rarely makes sense for one spare key you could cut yourself on your next errand.
bullets: Bring the original key, not a copy, for the most accurate cut
Test the new key in every lock it should open before you leave the area
If the copy feels stiff, ask the store to clean up the cut edges

sections.heading: When a Mobile Service Is a Premium, Not a Necessity
paragraphs: Some customers simply prefer that we come to them: a busy schedule, a building full of tenants who all need keys, or limited mobility. That is a real service and we are glad to provide it, as long as everyone understands it is a convenience you are choosing, priced like any other on-site visit.
What we do not want is a customer who expected a five-dollar key and ended up surprised by a service-call bill. Knowing your options ahead of time is the best way to avoid that.

sections.heading: Keys a Hardware Store Usually Cannot Copy
paragraphs: There are cases where a hardware store is the wrong place. High-security and restricted keys, such as those from Medeco, Mul-T-Lock or similar systems, are protected by patents and key-control programs. They can only be cut by an authorized dealer, often with proof that you are allowed to order copies.

Keys stamped "Do Not Duplicate" for a business or apartment building should also go through the building owner or property manager. And if a key is badly worn, bent or cracked, a straight copy will carry the same wear into the new key. In that case the lock may need to be decoded and a fresh key cut to the correct factory depths.

sections.heading: When You Actually Need a Locksmith
paragraphs: Call a locksmith when you cannot get in, when you have no working key at all, or when the lock itself is the problem. These are jobs that need tools, skill and someone on site.
bullets: You are locked out of your home, office or car
You lost every key and have nothing left to copy
You moved in, a roommate moved out, or keys were stolen, and the lock should be rekeyed
A key broke off inside the lock or the lock no longer turns smoothly
You want a new deadbolt, smart lock or high-security lock installed

sections.heading: Think for a Minute Before You Call: It Saves Everyone Money
paragraphs: Here is something most customers never hear: for a local service business, every call costs money before anyone picks up a tool. Online ads and listing platforms charge for each lead, whether the call turns into a job or not. When many calls are for things that did not need a technician, those costs add up, and over time they push service prices up for everyone.

So before you search online and call the first company you see, take a minute to ask yourself whether you need someone on site, or whether a quick trip to the hardware store, a spare key from a family member, or a call to your building manager solves it. Many customers tell us afterward, "I didn't know that." Now you do, and you keep the money in your pocket.

None of this means you should wait when you truly need help. Locked out late at night, a door that will not lock, or no key at all? Call right away. That is exactly what we are here for, day and night.

sections.heading: Save the Service Call for the Work That Needs It
paragraphs: Lockman ASAP Locksmith serves homes and businesses across San Francisco day and night. We would rather earn your trust with honest advice than charge you for a trip you did not need. Copy your spare at the hardware store, keep it somewhere safe, and keep our number for the day the lock, not the key, is the problem.

faq.question: How much does it cost to copy a house key in San Francisco?
faq.answer: A standard house key copy at a hardware store usually costs around five to ten dollars. Ordering a mobile locksmith for the same copy costs more because it includes travel, arrival time and labor.

faq.question: Can a hardware store copy any key?
faq.answer: No. Restricted and high-security keys can only be cut by an authorized dealer, and keys marked "Do Not Duplicate" should go through the building owner or property manager.

faq.question: What if I have no key left to copy?
faq.answer: Then a hardware store cannot help. A locksmith can open the lock, rekey it or cut a new key by decoding the lock on site.

faq.question: Why does it matter if I call a locksmith for something simple?
faq.answer: Local businesses pay for every call that comes through online ads and listings. Calling only when you need a technician on site keeps your own cost down and helps keep service prices fair for everyone.
